event: Great Heathen Army invades – widespread Viking settlement begins across north and east England
Norman Conquest – William defeats Harold at Hastings; Normans seize control of land and government
William invites Jewish moneylenders to England to fund the crown
First Blood Libel stories begin in Norwich - increased anti-Semitism in England.
Edward I expels all Jews – over 3,000 forced into exile
Edward III invites Flemish Weavers to England - 27 turn Colchester from 53rd to 13th richest town.
St Bartholomew's Day Massacre – 30,000 Huguenots murdered in France; thousands flee to Protestant England
Cromwell allows Jews to return to England to escape European persecution
Charles II gives all Huguenots Denizen status - they create weaver town in Spitalfields.
Foreign Protestants Naturalisation Act – full citizenship for all European Protestants; ~13,000 Palatine refugees arrive
Slave Trade abolished – major shift in legal status of African and Caribbean migrants in Britain
Irish Famine begins – ~2 million flee Ireland; many settle in British industrial cities
Russian pogroms – ~150,000 Ashkenazi Jews flee to Britain; settle in Whitechapel, East End
Aliens Act – Britain's first law limiting migration; specifically targeting Ashkenazi Jewish immigrants
British Nationality Act – grants Commonwealth citizenship; Windrush Generation begins arriving in Britain
Notting Hill Race Riots – white mob of ~400 attacks black homes over five nights
Kelso Cochrane murdered; Claudia Jones organises first Caribbean Carnival at St Pancras Town Hall
Bristol Bus Boycott ends employment colour bar; Notting Hill Housing Trust founded
Race Relations Act – first British law banning racial discrimination in public life
Mangrove Nine protest and trial – judge recognises institutional racism in policing for the first time
Idi Amin expels ~27,000 Ugandan Asians; most settle in Britain
Maastricht Treaty – Britain agrees to free movement of people as part of the European Union
Tehran Conference – Grand Alliance agrees strategy; Stalin pleased by commitment to a second front (D-Day)
Yalta Conference – Germany divided into four zones; Stalin promises free elections in Eastern Europe – promise he immediately breaks
Potsdam Conference – atomic bomb dropped without telling Stalin; Grand Alliance collapses
Long Telegram and Novikov Telegram – both governments formally advised to treat each other as enemies
Truman Doctrine ($400m to Greece and Turkey) and Marshall Plan ($13bn to rebuild Western Europe)
Berlin Blockade – USSR closes all road and rail links; USA flies in 4,000 tonnes daily for 10 months
NATO formed as capitalist military alliance; Germany permanently divided into FRG (West) and GDR (East)
Warsaw Pact formed as communist military alliance – two armed camps now face each other across Europe
Hungarian Uprising – Khrushchev sends 1,000 tanks; 3,000 Hungarians killed; 20,000 flee; Nagy arrested
Khrushchev's Berlin Ultimatum - Gives West 6 months to leave Berlin following refugee crisis
Cuban Revolution - Castro overthrows General Batista and nationalises US-owned land in Cuba
Paris Summit - Eisenhower and Khruschev clash over U2 Spyplane incident - no agreement
Berlin Wall built 13 August – East Germany seals the border; families divided for 28 years
Cuban Missile Crisis – 13-day standoff; world closest to nuclear war; resolved by removing missiles
Hotline established between Moscow and Washington; Test Ban Treaty bans atmospheric nuclear tests
Prague Spring crushed – 500,000 Warsaw Pact troops invade Czechoslovakia; 70 killed; Dubček arrested
SALT 1 signed – Nixon and Brezhnev agree first nuclear arms limitation treaty; détente begins
Helsinki Accords agreed - European Borders; Human rights; Trade and scientifc co-operation.
USSR invades Afghanistan on Christmas Eve – détente ends; Second Cold War begins
Reagan announces SDI ("Star Wars") – threatens to make Soviet nuclear arsenal obsolete
Gorbachev becomes leader – introduces Perestroika and Glasnost; Cold War begins to thaw
Washington Summit - Reagan and Gorbachev agree INF Treaty to reduce nuclear weapons
Sinatra Doctrine replaces Brezhnev Doctrine – satellite states can "go their own way"
Berlin Wall falls 9 November – all satellite states abandon communism; Cold War ends
Gorbachev resigns Christmas Day; USSR dissolved; Cold War officially over
Elizabeth I becomes Queen – inherits £227,000 debt, religious division, war with France
Religious Settlement – Act of Supremacy and Act of Uniformity establish the Church of England
Treaty of Edinburgh – Scottish lords renounce Mary's claim to English throne; Mary refuses to ratify
Vestment Controversy - Archbishop Parker compromises with puritans that they can wear a plain white robe.
Mary Queen of Scots flees to England – imprisoned; becomes focal point for Catholic plots for 18 years
Revolt of the Northern Earls – Catholic rebellion fails; Elizabeth raises 14,000 soldiers; ~450 rebels hanged
Pope Pius V excommunicates Elizabeth – all Catholics encouraged to remove her from power
Ridolfi Plot uncovered – first major Catholic assassination plot; Duke of Norfolk executed
Vagabonds Act - Vagrants over 14 to be whipped and have hole burnt in ear.
Act for the Relief of the Poor - Houses of Creation established for able-bodied poor.
Drake's Circumnavigation - raids £400,000 of spanish treasure. Knighted by Elizabeth on the Golden Hind.
Throckmorton Plot uncovered; Bond of Association agreed – Privy Council pledges to kill anyone conspiring to benefit from Elizabeth's death
Treaty of Nonsuch – England officially goes to war with Spain to support Dutch Revolt.
Virginia colony - Two attempts are made to colonise Roanoke island. Both fail.
Babington Plot – Walsingham obtains Mary's written approval of assassination plans
Mary Queen of Scots executed after Babington Plot; her written complicity proved by Walsingham
Spanish Armada defeated – fireships at Calais, Battle of Gravelines, storms destroy over half the fleet
Kaiser abdicates; Ebert declares Weimar Republic; armistice signed 11 November – "Dolchstoss" myth begins
Spartacist revolt – Luxemburg leads 100,000 workers; crushed by Freikorps; Luxemburg killed
Treaty of Versailles – £6.6bn reparations, 13% land lost, army limited to 100,000, 100% war guilt
Kapp Putsch – Freikorps seize Berlin; defeated by workers' general strike after 3 days
Hyperinflation crisis – bread costs 200 billion marks; Munich Putsch fails; Hitler jailed
Rentenmark introduced – halts hyperinflation; tied to land value not printed money
Dawes Plan – reparations cut to £50m/year; $200m US loans secured; Weimar recovery begins
Hindenburg elected President; Locarno Pact – Germany accepts Versailles borders; France leaves the Ruhr
Bamberg Conference - Hitler cements Nazi party as Far-Right party focused on elections, not violent revolution.
Wall Street Crash – US loans recalled; German unemployment reaches 6 million by 1933
Nazis win 230 seats – become largest party in the Reichstag
Hitler appointed Chancellor – Von Papen's fatal miscalculation; "Mouse in my pocket"
Reichstag Fire – 4,000 Communists arrested; Communists banned from 81 seats; Nazis get 2/3 majority
Enabling Act – Hitler gains power to make laws without the Reichstag; democracy legally abolished
Night of the Long Knives – Röhm and ~400 others murdered; army's loyalty secured
Hindenburg dies – Hitler becomes Führer; combines Chancellor and President; army swears personal oath
Nuremberg Laws – Jews stripped of German citizenship; banned from marrying non-Jews
Berlin Olympics - Huge celebration of German nationalism - Jesse Owens wins 4 Gold medals.
Marriage loans are cancelled - rearmament means more men in the army. Women encouraged into factories.
Kristallnacht – thousands of synagogues and businesses destroyed; over 100 Jews killed; 30,000 arrested
